claim: Robert E. Lee, commander of the Confederate States Army during the American Civil War, was not a slave owner.
justification: High-confidence evidence (confidence 0.90) shows Robert E. Lee assumed managerial control over enslaved people through his role as executor of the Custis estate and was listed as an agent or manager in the 1860 Census, indicating his active involvement in slavery. Additionally, confidence 0.85 evidence from mainstream historians characterizes Lee as an active enslaver who benefited from slavery. While some evidence suggests he did not hold legal title to enslaved individuals, the knowledge from these trustworthy sources explicitly refutes the claim that Lee was not a slave owner, as he exercised control and oversight akin to ownership.
